text: Sourdough starter is a culture of wild yeast and lactic bacteria that is fed with flour and water every day.
A mature starter doubles in size within six hours after feeding and smells pleasantly sour.
Bread dough needs a long fermentation at a cool temperature to develop flavour and an open crumb.
Shaping the loaf builds surface tension, which helps the bread rise upward in the oven.
Baking in a covered iron pot traps steam and gives the crust a crackling shine.
Stale bread can be turned into crumbs, croutons or a savoury pudding.
A sloop carries one mast with a mainsail and a jib and is easy to handle for a small crew.
Sailing close to the wind means pointing the bow as near to the wind as the sails allow.
The keel keeps the boat from sliding sideways and its ballast stops the boat from capsizing.
Reefing the mainsail reduces the sail area when the wind grows strong.
Tides and currents decide the safe time to enter a narrow harbour.
A lifejacket and a safety line are required for every sailor on deck at night.
Jupiter is the largest planet of the solar system and has a great red storm.
The four large moons of Jupiter were discovered by Galileo with an early telescope.
A refracting telescope bends light with a lens while a reflecting telescope collects light with a mirror.
A light year is the distance that light travels in one year, about nine trillion kilometres.
Stars end their life as white dwarfs, neutron stars or black holes depending on their mass.
The Milky Way is a spiral galaxy that contains hundreds of billions of stars.
Pressure is force per unit area and is measured in pascals.
Atmospheric pressure at sea level is about one hundred thousand pascals, or one bar.
A barometer measures atmospheric pressure, and falling pressure often warns of a storm.
The volume of a gas at fixed temperature is inversely proportional to its pressure, a rule called Boyle's law.
Heating a gas in a closed vessel raises its pressure because the molecules move faster.
A pressure cooker raises the boiling point of water by raising the pressure inside the pot.
A honeybee colony has one queen, thousands of workers and a few hundred drones.
Workers communicate the direction of a flower patch with a waggle dance inside the hive.
A beekeeper inspects the frames every week in summer to look for brood and stores of honey.
Smoke calms the bees because it masks the alarm signal that guards release.
Honey is extracted by spinning the uncapped frames in a centrifuge.
In winter the bees form a tight cluster and shiver to keep the queen warm.
A volcano forms where molten rock called magma rises through the crust and erupts as lava.
Shield volcanoes have gentle slopes because their runny lava spreads far before it cools.
Explosive eruptions throw ash high into the atmosphere and can cool the climate for a year.
Seismographs detect small earthquakes that often come before an eruption.
The Pacific ring of fire holds most of the active volcanoes on earth.
Volcanic soil is rich in minerals and supports vineyards and tea gardens.
In chess each player starts with sixteen pieces, and the goal is to checkmate the opposing king.
The knight moves in an L shape and is the only piece that can jump over others.
Controlling the centre of the board with pawns gives the pieces more room to move.
Castling moves the king to safety and brings a rook into play in a single move.
An endgame with a king and a rook against a lone king is won by forcing the king to the edge.
A fork is a tactic in which one piece attacks two enemy pieces at the same time.
A solar panel converts sunlight into direct current using layers of silicon.
An inverter changes direct current from the panels into alternating current for the household.
Panels produce less power when shaded, so installers avoid trees and chimneys on the roof.
A battery stores surplus energy from the afternoon for use in the evening.
Feed-in tariffs pay households for the electricity they send back to the grid.
Panel efficiency falls slowly, about half a percent each year, over their lifetime.
A marathon is a race of forty-two kilometres and one hundred and ninety-five metres.
Most training plans build the weekly distance slowly and include one long run at an easy pace.
Runners eat carbohydrates the evening before a race to fill the glycogen stores in their muscles.
Hitting the wall describes the sudden fatigue that comes when glycogen runs out.
Good running shoes cushion the heel and should be replaced after about eight hundred kilometres.
Tapering means cutting the training volume in the last two weeks before the race.
Espresso is made by forcing hot water through finely ground coffee at high pressure.
A coarse grind suits the French press because the grounds steep in the water for four minutes.
Fresh beans taste best within a month after roasting, before the aroma fades.
Water for brewing should be just below boiling, at around ninety-three degrees.
A pour over filter drips slowly and gives a clean cup with little sediment.
Decaffeinated coffee has most of the caffeine removed with water or a solvent before roasting.
